robots.name: Threehalves
robots.description: A centaur-like body combines four legs, two arms and a goat head. A striking example of deliberately moving beyond human anatomy.
robots.reality: Development concept focused on teleoperating skilled work in dangerous environments; no verified consumer release.
robots.reason: Intended to keep people away from dangerous physical work, rather than share domestic life.
robots.identification: The drawing links directly to Satyress. The manufacturer names this design Threehalves.

robots.name: BabyAlpha
robots.description: A dog-shaped robot with an animated face, voice interaction and family-oriented play.
robots.reality: Manufacturer offers a purchase route. Availability, language support and shipping depend on region; the drawing also links to a Kickstarter campaign.
robots.reason: Designed around ongoing family interaction and pet-like attachment.
robots.identification: Matches WEILAN BabyAlpha; directly corroborated by the Kickstarter link in the drawing.

robots.name: Moya
robots.description: A human-proportioned android with a realistic face and skin, aimed at social interaction.
robots.reality: Publicly demonstrated. Broad consumer delivery and unsupervised care capabilities are not established by the sources checked.
robots.reason: Its human appearance and proposed companionship role imply sustained social contact, not proven clinical care.
robots.identification: The image itself names Moya and shows DroidUp branding. The maker catalog supports its biomimetic work; no retail availability verified.

robots.name: Goat-costumed quadruped
robots.description: A quadruped wearing a realistic mountain-goat shell. The costume changes how people encounter an otherwise mechanical platform.
robots.reality: The exact base robot and costume supplier are unverified. It may use a Unitree Go2, but that is not a confirmed identification.
robots.reason: A public novelty and encounter; the picture alone cannot establish a home-companion role.
robots.identification: A costumed robot dog at Davos is supported by event context. Unitree Go2 is only a possible base; retained as an unresolved variant, not a separate confirmed product.

robots.name: Reachy 2
robots.description: An expressive head, antennae and two arms on an omnidirectional base. An approachable platform for learning manipulation.
robots.reality: Developer and research platform with Python control and VR teleoperation. A lab platform does not arrive as a turnkey household helper.
robots.reason: Built to explore tasks in human spaces such as homes, offices and hospitals.
robots.identification: Reachy family is clear from the head and antennae. The mobile dual-arm configuration is consistent with Reachy 2; exact revision is not explicit in the image.

robots.name: Reachy Mini
robots.description: A small expressive desktop robot with moving antennae and a camera.
robots.reality: Orderable maker kit in wireless and tethered versions. Experiences depend on installed apps; it cannot perform physical household chores.
robots.reason: A persistent conversational and playful presence at a desk.
robots.identification: Identified by its distinctive head and antennae and the direct product link in the drawing.

robots.name: Mirokaï · Miroki
robots.description: A fictional character with an animated face, arms and a rolling-ball base. Designed for interaction and assistance in shared human spaces.
robots.reality: First commercial deployments are open. The maker reports a senior-living pilot; autonomy continues to develop. This is not a patient-lifting robot.
robots.reason: Repeated conversation and engagement with residents, patients and staff bring it closer than a delivery-only robot.
robots.identification: The orange character is Miroki, one of the Mirokaï family. The drawing directly links to Enchanted Tools.

robots.name: Galbot G1
robots.description: A two-armed semi-humanoid with an articulated lifting body and mobile base, used for handling everyday goods.
robots.reality: The manufacturer describes retail and medical-service deployments. Pharmacy logistics should not be equated with personal nursing care.
robots.reason: Primarily supports the service a person receives; close physical caregiving is not evidenced.
robots.identification: The broad visor, elongated white chest and folding lower structure are consistent with Galbot G1. The cropped image hides the base, so the exact match remains provisional.

robots.name: Sprout
robots.description: A small humanoid with a soft exterior, expressive eyebrows and a deliberately friendly, nonhuman face.
robots.reality: Creator Edition is offered as a developer platform. It is a foundation for building applications, not evidence of a finished domestic care service.
robots.reason: Designed to interact naturally in spaces occupied by people; social presence is central to the design.
robots.identification: Both the pasted yellow robot and the remotely embedded product image depict Sprout. Counted once, with both images preserved.

robots.name: NEO · early design
robots.description: A soft-suited humanoid designed to take on household chores and interact through voice.
robots.reality: Current NEO has an early-access order route and foundational autonomy. Unfamiliar chores can use scheduled remote expert assistance. The reference shows an earlier design.
robots.reason: Intended to live in a household and participate in everyday routines; social proximity is not proof of care competence.
robots.identification: The suit and face resemble the NEO Beta-era design. The status here refers to the current NEO program, not the pictured revision.

robots.name: Apollo
robots.description: A human-scale platform with a friendly minimal face, exposed mechanics and a chest display.
robots.reality: Its initial focus is manufacturing and logistics. Long-term general-purpose ambitions do not make it a current home robot.
robots.reason: Included as an industrial boundary reference from the drawing, not part of the personal-life core.
robots.identification: Visual match to the product or product family. Exact hardware revision may differ from the current catalog.

robots.name: Optimus

robots.reality: Tesla describes a development program. A broadly available consumer home robot is not established by the checked source.

robots.identification: Tesla lettering and the characteristic black head identify Optimus. Generation is not treated as certain from this crop.

robots.reason: Short exchanges in shared public spaces rather than ongoing household life.

robots.name: ElliQ

robots.name: Saros Z70

robots.name: Automower

robots.reality: A configurable research platform with navigation and manipulation tools. Application development is required for useful household tasks.
robots.reason: Explores everyday assistance and manipulation in spaces shared with people.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: ARI
robots.description: A mobile humanoid with expressive eyes, arms and a torso display for human–robot interaction.
robots.reality: Offered as a social robotics platform; assistive-living projects are research applications, not proof of an autonomous care service.
robots.reason: Ongoing social engagement and assistive interaction motivate its placement in the bonds ring.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Stretch
robots.description: A compact wheeled robot with a telescoping arm and gripper, designed to reach everyday objects.
robots.reality: Commercial research hardware; this photo shows Stretch 3, while the maker now also offers Stretch 4. Autonomous skills and assistive deployments require integration.
robots.reason: Physical assistance with everyday objects can share routines without a humanoid body.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: temi
robots.description: A screen on a mobile base that follows users, travels between saved places and supports video calls.
robots.reality: Sold for personal and business applications. A remote caller supplies the human presence in telepresence mode; autonomy mainly concerns movement.
robots.reason: Supports recurring communication and navigation in homes, offices and care settings.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Double 3
robots.description: A self-balancing video-call robot that lets a remote person move around an office or classroom.
robots.reality: The official site currently says Sold Out. Existing product documentation remains available; new-unit availability and ongoing service must be checked.
robots.reason: Shares meetings and classes as a remote person’s presence, rather than simulating its own personality.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: OriHime
robots.description: A small avatar robot with movable head and arms, operated remotely to let a person participate from elsewhere.
robots.reality: A telepresence system. The voice, intentions and gestures belong to a human operator; this entry covers the small OriHime, not the larger OriHime-D.
robots.reason: Enables shared daily activities and relationships with a distant human, rather than attachment to an autonomous character.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Obi
robots.description: A tabletop robotic arm and divided food dish that bring selected bites to a user’s mouth.
robots.reality: An assistive device controlled through accessible switches, with setup and suitability requirements. The maker now presents Obi 3; the product family is counted once.
robots.reason: Supports a basic activity of daily living through close physical assistance, without asking to be treated as a creature.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Labrador Retriever
robots.description: A mobile, height-adjustable platform that carries loads and retrieves compatible trays in the home.
robots.reality: The maker’s availability page prioritizes Retriever Pro for care providers but still cites a Q2 2024 production target. Current fulfilment is unverified; the chart conservatively retains pilot status.
robots.reason: Designed to reduce everyday physical effort for people with mobility limitations; reliance is functional rather than social.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Human Support Robot

sources.title: Toyota · assistive purpose and developer community

robots.description: A compact mobile manipulator with a lifting body and arm for reaching and retrieving household objects.
robots.reality: Toyota’s research platform and developer-community work explore assistive tasks. It is not a generally available home-care appliance.
robots.reason: The intended use supports independent living, so the inner ring records an assistive goal rather than proven care autonomy.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Starship delivery robot
robots.description: A compact six-wheeled cargo robot that delivers food and goods on pedestrian routes.
robots.reality: Operates as a delivery service in selected areas; availability depends on local partners and operating zones.
robots.reason: Shares sidewalks and brief collection moments with people, not domestic life.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Serve delivery robot
robots.description: A wheeled delivery container with an eye-like front and a friendly public-facing design.
robots.reality: A commercially deployed delivery fleet in selected markets, with remote assistance available when needed.
robots.reason: A character-like appearance softens encounters with pedestrians while the relationship remains transactional.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Relay
robots.description: A mobile compartment robot for transporting items through hotels and hospitals.
robots.reality: Commercial deployments require site integration, including doors and elevators. The family is counted once across revisions.
robots.reason: People encounter it briefly for deliveries; hospital logistics are not direct caregiving.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: K5
robots.description: A tall mobile security robot that patrols sites and provides observations to security staff.
robots.reality: Offered as an autonomous security service with human operational oversight. It should not be read as an autonomous police officer.
robots.reason: Its primary human relationship is visible surveillance in shared spaces.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: Whiz
robots.description: An autonomous commercial vacuum that follows configured cleaning routes in occupied buildings.
robots.reality: A commercial cleaning product used with human cleaners and fleet management.
robots.reason: Performs background maintenance even when it is physically near people.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: ANYmal
robots.description: A four-legged inspection robot with visual, thermal and acoustic sensing for industrial facilities.
robots.reality: Commercial industrial inspection platform. Dog-like locomotion does not make it a robotic pet.
robots.reason: A boundary example that substitutes for hazardous or repetitive inspection work.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.

robots.name: CyberDog 2
robots.description: A compact dog-shaped quadruped combining locomotion, sensors and interactive behaviour.
robots.reality: Xiaomi publishes a product page and user manual. Market availability is regional; demonstrations do not establish a dependable autonomous pet.
robots.reason: Blends pet-like presentation with developer experimentation and shared activities.
robots.identification: Named and described by the manufacturer or originating research institution.
